newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stock exchange expands short sell list to 241.
newsitem.headline: HK stock exchange expands short sell list to 241.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong has expanded the list of designated securities that may be sold short to 241 from 112, the exchange said in a statement issued on Wednesday.
"We are trying to roll it out so that all stocks are in the list as soon as possible," said Paul Phenix, executive director of the exchange's Compliance division.

The expanded list included Hang Seng Index constituents, the constituent stocks of the Hang Seng China Enterprise Index, the 50 stocks in the Mid-Cap Index, the next 50 largest stocks and any stock with a derivative issued on it, said Phenix.
"The idea is to review the list (of stocks) and short selling trading every six months," said Phenix
As at the end of February 1997, there were 590 companies listed on the Hong Kong exchange and a total of 1,329 listed securities.
Phenix said the exchange would be looking at including warrants on the list of issues permitted for short selling.
"The problem with warrants is that there are rules on who can issue warrants and going short on a warrant is very similar to issuing a warrant, so this will require further study," he said.
The big international brokerage houses were the main participants in short selling in Hong Kong, Phenix said.
Short selling on the Hong Kong exchange took off slowing when it was first launched in early 1994.

The exchange's latest statistics show that in February 1997, only 26 stocks were sold short and total monthly short selling turnover was HK$2.20 billion, accounting for just 1.41 percent of total exchange turnover during the month.
But this was considerably greater than short selling turnover of HK$102.66 million in February 1995.
